clue.text: 1 under par that's ignored girlfriend …

indicators.note: ignored says the letters for the next phrase are left out of the golf score

parts.note: a birdie is a hole played in one stroke under par in golf
that's, or 'that is', is abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A golfer's lucky birdie is spoilt by a girlfriend being neglected, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The '1' is the number one here, not a cross-reference. BIRD is informal British slang for a girlfriend or young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang uses bird for a young woman, especially someone's sweetheart.

clue.text: … following her rejection, to embrace nice odd European

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: to embrace says the reversed pronoun wraps around the letters that follow
rejection turns the word her back on itself so it reads from right to left
odd picks the first, third and later odd-numbered letters of the word nice

explanation.surface: Carrying on from 1 down: after the girlfriend dumps someone, a nice but odd foreigner is taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 1 down's surface only; the clues are parsed separately. 'rejection' reverses HER to REH, and 'odd' picks the odd letters of 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of France is a European, so this nationality noun answers the clue word.

clue.text: With victory secured, Hector returned a hero

indicators.note: secured means held fast inside, so the victory letter is locked within the rearranged letters
to hector is to bully or push about, so the following letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: V is the familiar abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign

explanation.surface: Hector of Troy comes home triumphant, a hero after winning the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector looks like the Trojan prince but is the anagram signal: RETURNED A rearranges to ADENTURER, and 'secured' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer is a bold person who seeks out daring exploits, so a hero in the swashbuckling sense.

clue.text: Wine regularly drunk by young men and women

indicators.note: drunk by says the letters are swallowed inside the word for young men

parts.note: lads are boys or young men

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word Wine, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: At a party, the wine is being knocked back by both the young men and the women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes I and E from 'Wine'; 'drunk by' puts them inside LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies is a polite plural term for women, as in a toilet sign.

clue.text: Novel writer encapsulates dreadful pirate sacking island

indicators.note: encapsulates means holds within, so the writing implement wraps around the rest

parts.note: a pen is something you write with

indicators.note: dreadful says the remaining letters of the word pirate are in a terrible jumble
sacking means dismissing, so the island letter is thrown out of the word pirate

parts.note: I is the usual abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A writer's novel contains a dreadful pirate who goes about sacking an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'sacking' sound like pillage, but here it means dismissing: the island letter leaves 'pirate', and 'dreadful' rearranges PRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's tale of the boy who never grows up appeared as a novel as well as a stage play.

clue.text: Turkish commander has a good laugh

parts.note: ha is the written sound of a laugh

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer is enjoying a good chuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: An agha was an Ottoman title for a military officer or chief, so a Turkish commander.

clue.text: Ground in supreme authority

parts.note: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London
in, meaning fashionable, can also be hip

explanation.surface: A short legal phrase: some territory is held under the highest power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like land under the authority, but it is the London cricket ground LORD'S. 'In' means trendy, giving HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordship means sovereignty or dominion, the rule exercised by a supreme power over people or land.

clue.text: Fruit are squished when put under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something under places it below, so the jumbled letters come after the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the scientific symbol for pressure

indicators.note: squished means squashed out of shape, so the letters of are get rearranged

explanation.surface: Soft fruit gets squashed when weighed down by pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squished' rearranges ARE to EAR; 'put under' puts that below P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a familiar orchard fruit, an example of the general category.

clue.text: Short of time, Rita tried a broken shed light

indicators.note: broken says the remaining letters are smashed and reassembled
short of means lacking, so a time letter is taken away from the phrase

explanation.surface: Running late, Rita attempts to use a broken garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' removes one T from RITA TRIED A, and 'broken' rearranges the nine letters left. 'shed' looks like a garden hut, but here it is a verb in 'shed light'.
explanation.definitionFit: To irradiate is to illuminate or cast rays upon something, so to shed light on it.

clue.text: 1 retiring, say, getting very old

definitions.note: the clue at 1 down is a bird, and this is one kind

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
getting means receiving, so the abbreviation for say takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: say, meaning for example, is abbreviated e.g.
so can mean very, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: A bird is going off to retire as it grows very old.
explanation.walkthrough: Several clues in this puzzle use 1, the answer at 1 down, to mean 'a bird', and all of them are birds from 'The Twelve Days of Christmas'. 'getting' and then 'retiring' make ESOOG and read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a large waterfowl, an example of a bird; six geese a-laying feature in the carol.

clue.text: Play English actor

definitions.meaning: to play lightly, as sunlight flickers and moves about over water
Charles ... is an English actor, known for Game of Thrones

explanation.surface: A theatre listing: a play with an English actor in it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol, the ten ladies are dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To play can mean to move lightly and quickly, as light does over a surface; Charles Dance is the English screen actor.

clue.text: European brewing cider over spirit

indicators.note: over means covering on both sides here, so the jumbled letters sit round the word for spirit
brewing means being made or stirred up, so the letters of cider are rearranged

parts.note: elan means flair, dash or spirit

explanation.surface: A European is making cider and pouring it over some liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges CIDER to IC...DER, which goes 'over' ELAN. Here 'spirit' means verve rather than a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iceland, the North Atlantic nation, is a European.

clue.text: Bill really doesn't like Aeneas's companion

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
to detest something is to really not like it

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill can't stand the hero of Virgil's epic's sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid, the faithful friend who travels with the Trojan hero is named Achates.

clue.text: Dad dancing — extremely liable to confuse!

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of Dad are rearranged
extremely takes the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word liable

explanation.surface: Watching a father's embarrassing dancing is very likely to bewilder you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges DAD to ADD; 'extremely' takes L and E from 'liable'.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or befuddle the mind, which is to bewilder it.

clue.text: Spooner's timid father finds food store

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: shy means timid
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A bashful dad goes out and discovers a shop selling food.
explanation.walkthrough: SHY POP with its opening sounds swapped becomes PIE SHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that sells pastry pies is one kind of store selling food.

clue.text: Leaving Earth on holiday? Take in Uranus at the beginning

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the Earth letter comes first
take in means contain, so the holiday word swallows the planet's letter

parts.note: a vacation is a holiday

indicators.note: at the beginning takes the opening letter of the word Uranus

explanation.surface: A space tourist leaves Earth for a holiday and drops in on Uranus first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the beginning' gives U from 'Uranus'; 'Take in' puts it inside VACATION, and 'on' sets E above that.
explanation.definitionFit: Evacuation is the act of leaving or vacating a place, often for safety.

clue.text: 1p + 1p? Er …

parts.note: one penny is written 1p, and P alone stands for a penny
here the figure 1 is read as the letter I it looks like, with p after it
taken as the hesitant sound, as written

explanation.surface: Someone doing simple sums with pennies hesitates over the total.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate definition: the answer is one of the eleven pipers piping in 'The Twelve Days of Christmas', the puzzle's theme, so the whole clue stands for it. The first penny gives only P; in the second, 1 reads as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes, and the carol's eleventh day brings pipers piping, the gift this themed clue points to.

clue.text: Duke finished port

parts.note: over means finished, as in 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: A nobleman has drunk the last of his port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine, but it means a harbour town. Dover is the English Channel ferry port; the carol's turtle doves are in the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover in Kent is England's busiest ferry harbour, a port on the Channel.

clue.text: Disciples are against books by stars

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Followers of a faith oppose scriptures being placed next to astrology.
explanation.definitionFit: Votaries are devoted followers or worshippers of a cause or deity, so disciples.

clue.text: 1 perhaps Rambo misses mother

definitions.note: the answer at 1 down is a bird, and this is an example of one

indicators.note: misses means fails to include, so the letters for mother drop out

parts.note: Rambo, the muscle-bound action hero, is a typical he-man
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An action hero fails to turn up to see his mum.
explanation.walkthrough: Rambo is not a name to use as it is: he stands for HE-MAN, a macho type. Three French hens appear in the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female chicken, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Exhausted, like "la" or "te"?

definitions.meaning: worn out to the point of collapse
each is one half of the four-letter word late, which means deceased

explanation.surface: Someone tired out after singing the notes of the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: La and te look like the musical scale, but they are the two halves of LATE, which means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tired out is informally described as feeling barely alive, nearly at the point of collapse.

clue.text: A quiet, posh prime minister backing increase in intensity …

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the three pieces after the article are read in reverse

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
U stands for upper class, so posh

explanation.surface: A quiet, upper-class prime minister's support is growing stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses P, U and PM to give MPUP after A. 'backing' looks like support, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To amp something up is to make it more intense, an idiom from turning up an amplifier.

clue.text: … then wildly runs by a large entrance

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of then are flung into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: Carrying on from 20, a big crowd then rushes wildly past the large doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges THEN to ENTH. 'entrance' looks like a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate or spellbind, which is the verb sense of entrance.

clue.text: REM comeback follows band's finale with strange musician

indicators.note: finale means the closing part, so the last letter of the word band is taken

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd

indicators.note: comeback means coming back, so the group name REM is read backwards

explanation.surface: The rock group REM make a comeback after a band's odd final number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' reverses REM to MER. RUM is old British slang for odd. Twelve drummers drumming appear in the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer is a musician who plays the drums.

clue.text: Inside, doctors are cooking quails

indicators.note: inside says the jumbled letters go within the abbreviation for doctors

parts.note: DDs are Doctors of Divinity

indicators.note: cooking means being prepared or fiddled, so the letters of are are rearranged

explanation.surface: Physicians are roasting the small game birds called quails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quails' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to shrink in fear. 'cooking' rearranges the letters of 'are' to REA. DDs are Doctors of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, and to dread is likewise to fear greatly.

clue.text: Might she wear tights having no runs?

definitions.meaning: a young unmarried woman, the sort who might wear tights
in cricket, an over in which no runs are scored has this name

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman wears tights without ladders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like ladders in tights, but it means cricket runs: an over with no runs scored is a maiden. Maids a-milking appear in the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old word for a girl or young unmarried woman, and a cricket term for an over in which no runs are scored.

clue.text: 1 fictional TV and radio presenter? Aha!

definitions.meaning: the solution at 1 down is a bird, and this is one kind

definitions.text: fictional TV and radio presenter? Aha!
definitions.meaning: Alan ..., Steve Coogan's comic broadcaster, whose catchphrase is 'Aha!'

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a made-up broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Partridge is a British comedy character, a clumsy radio and TV host whose catchphrase is 'Aha!'. The partridge in a pear tree begins the carol that supplies the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A partridge is a game bird; Alan Partridge is Steve Coogan's comic broadcaster, famous for saying 'Aha!'.

clue.text: Party to develop a "Third Way"

indicators.note: Party to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political party sets out to create a 'Third Way', a centrist policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a political party, but 'Party to' means sharing in the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a route or course of action, which is what a way means here.

clue.text: 22 across's endless call

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter, so the drummer's name is cut short

parts.note: the famous percussionist answering 22 across is the Beatle Ringo Starr

explanation.surface: A musician's never-ending shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 across is a drummer, and the famous one meant is Ringo Starr. Five gold rings appear in the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to telephone, and a ring is a phone call, as in 'give me a ring'.

clue.text: Jollies undress from top to bottom

indicators.note: from top to bottom says the first letter is moved to the end

parts.note: to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: Fun-seekers strip off every stitch of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the start of STRIP moves to the end. 'Jollies' is British slang for pleasure outings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jollies, in British slang, are pleasure jaunts or outings, which are also called trips.

clue.text: 1 small and pale

definitions.note: the light at 1 down is a bird, and this is an example of one

parts.note: wan means pale

explanation.surface: A short description: someone or something little and pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven swans a-swimming appear in the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan is a large white waterbird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Wooden old actor takes final curtain …

parts.note: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a Victorian actor-manager

indicators.note: final takes the last letter of the word curtain

explanation.surface: A stiff, wooden old actor takes his last curtain call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a critic's insult for the actor, but it is the definition. Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian London actor. The carol's pear tree is in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen is an old word for small household objects made of wood, used as an adjective meaning wooden.

clue.text: … with artist hugging endless comedy stars

parts.note: and can mean with, as in 'fish and chips'

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the artist's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

indicators.note: endless removes the first and last letters of the word comedy

explanation.surface: Continuing from 28, a painter embraces never-ending comedy celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips the ends off 'comedy' to leave OMED, which RA is 'hugging'. 'stars' looks like comedy celebrities, but it means the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation in the northern sky, a named group of stars.
